rationale: Resubmission of the three-times-accepted stream, re-verified as optimal. Loop j (N/16=2) outer, i (M/16=3) inner: both B tiles for column block j stay resident in scratchpad rows 16-47 across all three m-tiles, so each of the 4 B tiles loads exactly once (4 mvins). The single remaining scratchpad tile slot (row 0) forces 2 A-tile loads per output tile (12 A mvins). 16 tiles x 256 = 4096 DMA input bytes is provably minimal: 2A+2B residency needs 64 rows > 48; 2A+1B gives 18 loads (6 A + 12 B = 4608 bytes) since each B tile serves 3 m-tiles while each A tile serves only 2 n-tiles; and carrying an A tile across the j phases while keeping both B tiles resident would require 4 simultaneous slots (2 persistent B + carried A + one rotating A per k-step), exceeding the 48-row scratchpad. Since the 16-row accumulator holds exactly one tile, each output tile's two k-steps must be adjacent: overwrite compute for k=0 (out_addr bit 30 clear), accumulate compute for k=1 (bit 30 set), then immediate mvout. Every compute gets its own preload (accumulated=false, bd_spad_addr=GARBAGE_ADDR) as each compute consumes its pending preload. K=32 satisfies 32*16384 <= 2147483647; all reductions proceed in increasing k order per output tile. Expanded commands: 4 config + 16 mvin + 12 preload + 12 compute + 6 mvout + 1 fence = 51, minimal per class given the 16 mandatory tile loads.
